request: Casting an ability takes twice its listed mana cost. A successful cast should charge the listed cost once; a rejected cooldown recast must not spend more mana or extend its cooldown. Reproduce and fix this using actual arena casts.
analysis: Combat.BeginCast subtracts twice ChampionKit.Mana at line 106. This is a suspected cause pending actual arena execution. Morgana E lists 70 mana and a 14-second cooldown. The scenario checks its successful shield cast, immediate and delayed cooldown rejections, and an independent Ahri Q cast costing 55 mana. Mana comparisons around rejected casts exclude regeneration by comparing checkpoints without advancing time between them.

reviewReason: The report explicitly requires one listed mana charge per successful arena cast and preservation of mana and cooldown on rejected recasts. ChampionKit lists Morgana E at 70 mana and 14 seconds, and Ahri Q at 55 mana. DexArena.Cast invokes BeginCast and creates the shield or projectile; BeginCast currently subtracts twice the listed cost. The trace reproduces both double charges while showing both cooldown recasts preserve resources. The proposed checks follow from the report and source, use actual casts, and account for regeneration by comparing immediately adjacent checkpoints. Shield and projectile assertions provide successful-cast controls. These checks cover this scenario only.

patchExplanation: The supplied arena observations show Morgana E spending 140 mana and Ahri Q spending 110, while cooldown rejection checks pass. Combat.BeginCast explicitly subtracts twice ChampionKit.Mana. Remove that multiplier so accepted casts charge the listed cost once, preserving existing validation, cooldowns, and ability effects. Host replay is required to verify the proposal.
completionReason: The frozen reproduction failed before source editing and passed after compilation. A separate, frozen specification witness failed before and passed in a fresh Play session afterward. Protected core/arena regressions and saved scenarios passed; protected host hashes are unchanged. Expected behavior is model-reviewed against the report, not independently human-certified.
